title: Multi-signal autoscaler evaluation and outcomes (signal fusion)
summary: This sheet captures a 3-week evaluation of a multi-signal autoscaling policy that fuses utilization, queue depth, tail-latency, and predicted arrival-rate signals into a probabilistic scale decision. Goal: reduce cold starts and SLO breaches while limiting steady-state waste compared to our baseline min/max hysteresis autoscaler.
experiment_goal: Validate that signal fusion + small stochastic smoothing can reduce 99th pct latency SLO violations and cold-start counts by >=30% with <=8% steady-state GPU idle increase across EU and us-west fleets.
hypothesis: Combining orthogonal signals (util + qlen + tail-latency + arrival forecast) with a weighted voting ensemble and short randomized backoff will trigger earlier scale-ups for transient spikes and delay scale-downs for recovering workloads, improving SLOs with modest cost impact.
experiment_design: Three policy variants (Fusion-A, Fusion-B, Fusion-C) vs Baseline. Each ran for 72h in parallel on dedicated shadow capacity slices per region (eu-west-1 and us-west-2). Traffic replay used production traces sampled from May 2026 (weekday peak + weekend). Key knobs: voting threshold, signal weights, random backoff distribution, min_pool per shard, prewarm buffer. Autoscaler operated at shard granularity (by model-size bin + region).
signals_and_weights: Signals: GPU_util (15s avg), queue_depth (1s sample), tail_latency_p95/p99 (sliding 60s), arrival_rate_forecast (10s EWMA), cold_start_rate (per-model counter). Example weights tested: {util:0.25, qlen:0.35, tail:0.25, arrival:0.15} and alternative skewed profiles. Fusion decision computes weighted score then compares to scale thresholds; separate logic for scale-up vs scale-down with asymmetric hysteresis.
policy_variants: Baseline: min/max + hysteresis (existing). Fusion-A: equalized weights, deterministic threshold, 30s cooldown. Fusion-B: qlen-heavy weights, randomized backoff ~Uniform(5s,20s) on scale-down. Fusion-C: forecast-amplified (arrival weight doubled), prewarm small ephemeral GPUs for predicted spikes. All Fusion variants respect per-shard min_pool and region capacity caps.
regions_and_fleet_config: eu-west-1: 160 GPUs reserved for experiment (A100/80G mix), us-west-2: 200 GPUs (80G + 40G mixture). Shards: small (7B models) mapped to 1 GPU nodes, large (70B+) mapped to 4-GPU nodes. Prewarm buffer sizes: 2%/4% of region fleet for Fusion-C. Spot-backed auxiliary pool used in us-west-2 only for burst recovery (cold-start risk mitigation).
workloads_tested: 1) PLG chat (burst traffic from feature launch), 2) nightly batch embedding jobs (steady high-throughput), 3) unpredictable conference demo spikes (short, high QPS), 4) mixed steady + bursts from multiple customers (multi-tenant stress). Each workload run used 24–72 hour windows with throughput multipliers to stress tails.
decision_logic_description: Per-shard score S = sum(w_i * normalized(signal_i)). Scale-up if S > U_threshold OR qlen > q_thresh. Scale-down if S < D_threshold AND no tail-latency excursions in last 90s. Randomized delay applied to scale-down to avoid synchronized drains. Separate emergency scale-out path: if p99 tail-latency > 1.5x SLO AND arrival_rate spike > 2x forecast, open emergency burst pool (spot) if available.
metrics_tracked: p50/p95/p99 latency, cold_start_count, scale_up_events, scale_down_events, time_to_add_capacity (s), steady_state_gpu_idle_pct, added_gpus_hours, cost_delta_estimate ($), SLO_breach_minutes, emergency_burst_usage_hours
raw_results_highlights: - Fusion-B reduced p99 SLO-breach minutes by 41% vs Baseline in eu-west-1 during weekday peak windows. - Cold starts fell 38% (Fusion-C best) due to prewarm + forecast path. - Steady-state idle increased 6.2% on average (Fusion-A) and 9.1% for Fusion-C; cost modeling shows Fusion-C cost +7% gross but net cost per successful request improved due to fewer retries. - Randomized backoff cut oscillatory scale-churn by ~52% across both regions. - Emergency burst pool used twice in us-west-2; spot init latency contributed 22s median additional time but prevented extended p99 spikes.

variant | p99_slo_minutes | cold_starts | steady_idle_pct | scale_churn_events_per_hour | cost_delta_pct
Baseline | 120 | 84 | 4.1% | 13.4 | 0%

cost_impact_estimate: Simple model: delta_cost = steady_idle_delta * region_hourly_gpu_cost * hours + ephemeral_spot_costs + prewarm_delta. Using EU cost assumptions, Fusion-B projected +2.4% monthly cost for customer-facing fleets, offset by ~12% fewer SLO-related retries/mitigations (engineering ops labor + incident cost).
anomalies_and_outliers: - One 45-minute window in eu-west-1 where Fusion-A repeatedly failed to scale due to metric probe gap (monitoring pipeline delay). Root cause: transient metrics ingestion lag from a new exporter version. - Nightly embedding job patterns created long tails that arrival-forecast underestimated; Fusion-C prewarm helped but arrival model needs longer horizon for batch windows.
followups_and_actions: 1) Ship conservative rollout of Fusion-B to 10% of production shards for two weeks; monitor p99 and cold-starts. 2) Harden metrics ingestion: add fallback and local aggregator to reduce probe gaps. 3) Improve arrival_rate_forecast model to incorporate 10m horizon for batch windows. 4) Add a per-customer sensitivity flag to avoid prewarm for low-value tenants (cost control). 5) Run cost analysis including incident-reduction savings for finance review.
notes_to_self: This sheet intentionally mixes numeric summaries and observational notes for quick handoff. Keep Fusion-C as an engineering playbook for high-SLO tenants but default rollout should be Fusion-B. Watch for correlated scale-downs triggered at 03:00 UTC after DST transitions — possible clock drift in exporter. Create ticket to schedule follow-up A/B with longer-run traces.
